name: Heartroot Token
description: A small carved piece cut from the heartroot of an old Feywood tree — a household's anchor-tree, a temple's sacred grove, or a watcher-post's bonded sentinel. Each token retains a living connection to the cut-point on its parent tree, allowing one-direction message passage between the holder and anyone present at the parent tree. Tokens are issued by the household or institution whose tree they came from; they are not bought, traded, or commonly seen.
narrative_effects: The cut-point on the parent tree retains a living connection to the token. A message spoken or carved into the token travels to the cut-point and waits there until someone at the parent tree retrieves it. A reply travels back to the token along the same connection.
Each token holds one message at a time. While a message is unread at one end, no new message can be placed at that end. Both directions follow the same rule.

Acquiring a token implies relationship. Households issue them to family members, sworn retainers, and trusted envoys. A token in the hand of someone the household never gave it to is a security incident, not a windfall — and the messages it carries can be used by whoever holds it, including against the household.
Creation requires a druid bonded to the parent tree (a House druid, Heartwarden, or grove-druid recognized by the tree). The cut must be willing — trees that resist produce dead tokens.
Names follow the form 'token of <tree-location>': a Vaelaryn estate token, a Sacred Grove token, a Hollow Reed watcher-token. Each is bound to its specific tree.

mechanical_effect.trigger: held by any bearer who speaks or inscribes a message of roughly 30 seconds of speech or 150 written words
mechanical_effect.modifier: carries one message at a time to the parent tree's cut-point; replies travel back the same way
mechanical_effect.applies_to: passing a single short message between the token and the parent tree, in either direction; the message waits at its destination until retrieved
mechanical_effect.does_not_apply: real-time conversation, messages longer than the cap, contact with any tree other than the parent tree, contact when the token's slot already holds an unread message in the relevant direction, contact through hostile fae magic / continuity-shear / iron-warded ground / corrupted parent tree (narrator's call when relevant)
